title: Condensing Law of Security Information
abstract: arXiv:2611.17918v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Scaling laws indicate that the generalization error of a large language model (LLM) decreases monotonically with model size once data is sufficient, and the corollary that larger models outperform smaller ones is now widely accepted. We argue that this corollary fails in security: decisions there hinge on anomalous inputs, which are long-tailed (e.g., zero-day attacks) and therefore poorly served by likelihood fitting. Worse still, the capability brought about by scale (e.g., inferring the intended whole from a corrupted part) leads a LLM silently \emph{repair} the anomaly before any downstream security head ever sees it. We formalize this as a tradeoff between two quantities: the cognitive capability $K(W)=I(W;P)$ that a model holds about the world distribution, and the security-information retention $R(W)=\frac{I(Z;S)}{I(A;S)}$ that survives in its intermediate representation. translated_abstract: 缩放定律表明，在数据充足的情况下，大语言模型（LLM）的泛化误差随模型规模单调递减，“更大模型优于更小模型”这一推论现已被广泛接受。我们论证这一推论在安全领域并不成立：安全决策依赖于异常输入，而异常输入呈长尾分布（例如零日攻击），因此似然拟合难以有效处理此类输入。更糟糕的是，规模所带来的能力（例如从受损的部分推断出原本完整的整体）会使LLM在任何下游安全模块察觉之前就悄悄地“修复”异常。我们将这一现象形式化为两个量之间的权衡：模型对世界分布的认知能力 K(W)=I(W;P)，以及在其中间表示中得以保留的安全信息保持率 R(W)=I(Z;S)/I(A;S)。我们推导了三个信息论界来连接……
tldr: 本文指出缩放定律在安全领域失效——模型越强越会在下游安全模块察觉前“悄悄修复”异常输入，并首次将其形式化为认知能力与安全信息保持率之间的权衡，推导出三个信息论界。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that scaling laws fail in security—stronger LLMs silently "repair" anomalous inputs before downstream security heads detect them—and formalizes this as a tradeoff between cognitive capability K(W) and security-information retention R(W), deriving three information-theoretic bounds.
